title: Simple Energy to Unveil India's First Family Electric Scooter on September 2 as EV Startup Targets Mass Market
excerpt: The Bengaluru-based company expands beyond performance scooters into the family segment with India's longest-range EV technology.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Simple Energy will launch India's first family electric scooter on September 2, 2026.
  • The company claims to be the first Indian OEM to produce heavy rare earth-free electric motors.
  • Simple Ultra model offers a 400 km IDC range, the longest for any electric scooter in India.
  • The family scooter is expected to be priced between ₹90,000 and ₹1.10 lakh, competitive with petrol scooters.
  • Simple Energy sold approximately 6,038 electric vehicles in 2025, aiming for higher sales in 2026.
  • Simple Energy will unveil India's first family electric scooter on September 2, expanding into the mass-market segment.
  • The new scooter is designed for everyday riders and families, emphasizing practicality and advanced technology.
  • Simple Energy is known for its performance-oriented EVs, with the Simple Ultra boasting a range of 400 kilometers, the highest in India.
  • The family scooter is expected to be priced between ₹90,000 and ₹100,000, targeting value-driven customers.

From Performance to Practicality

Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler manufacturer Simple Energy announced on Wednesday that it will unveil its first family electric scooter on September 2, marking a strategic expansion from its performance-focused lineup into the mass-market segment that dominates India's two-wheeler industry.

The company said the new scooter has been developed through years of in-house research and engineering, reflecting its "first principles" approach to product development. While Simple Energy did not reveal specifications beyond the launch date, the scooter is described as being engineered for everyday riders and families, combining practicality with advanced technology.

The move follows the company's recent launch of the Simple Ultra, which offers an IDC range of 400 kilometres — the highest claimed by any electric scooter in India. The Simple One and Simple OneS models, with ranges up to 181 km and top speeds of 105 km/h, established the company's reputation for performance-oriented EVs.

A Technology-First Approach

Simple Energy has positioned itself as a technology company that happens to make scooters. The company claims to be the first Indian original equipment manufacturer to commercially manufacture heavy rare earth-free electric motors — a significant differentiator amid supply-chain volatility in rare earth materials largely sourced from China.

Its R&D capabilities span proprietary software, vehicle technologies, and advanced engineering solutions, including in-house development of motors, battery management systems, and related components. The company recently launched its Gen 2 vehicle variants, which co-founder Shreshth Mishra described as targeting "value-driven customers" with enhanced range, performance, and usability.

Competitive Pricing in a Growing Market

Industry estimates suggest the family scooter will be priced between ₹90,000 and ₹1.10 lakh (ex-showroom), putting it within striking distance of popular petrol scooters. At that price point, the lower running costs of an electric scooter — typically ₹0.15-0.20 per km versus ₹2-3 per km for petrol — could make the total cost of ownership compelling for budget-conscious families.

Simple Energy sold approximately 6,038 units of its electric vehicles in 2025 and expects the new models to drive significantly higher sales in 2026.

Simple Energy's Market Strategy
›First family electric scooter launch on September 2, 2026.
›Focus on practical design for everyday riders and families.
›Competing against Ather Energy's EL01 model in a crowded market.
›Technology-first approach aims to enhance range and usability.

The company is backed by angel investors and family offices, including those connected to Apar Industries and Dr. A. Velumani.

What's Next

The September 2 unveil will compete for attention in an increasingly crowded Indian EV two-wheeler market. Ather Energy is expected to launch its EL01 model around August 29 at a similar price point. Simple Energy's family scooter will need to differentiate on range, build quality, and after-sales service — areas where the company's technology-first approach could prove decisive for Indian families considering their first electric vehicle.
